key_insight: Sequential magnetic alignment and liquid-metal bridging create vertical heat pathways in a soft composite while preserving lateral electrical insulation.
engineering_relevance: The composite offers a compliant thermal interface for skin-conformal electronics, thermoelectric generators, and wearable heat-spreading pads.
method: Magnetically align Ni microparticles in air before polymer infiltration to form densely packed vertical pathways.
Infiltrate a liquid-metal/Ni mixture into the scaffold to bridge interparticle gaps and reduce thermal resistance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports through-plane thermal conductivity of 7.5 W/(m K), lateral electrical conductivity below 10⁻¹² S/m, and mechanical compliance characterized by approximately 160 kPa.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether thermal performance and electrical insulation persist under repeated stretching.
paper_title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics
